messages:
acme-sre: Hi, after rotating our certs this morning, a bunch of internal services can't call the private Redwood API. We get TLS verify errors from our app hosts.

sam: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a short `curl -v` output from a failing host?

acme-sre: Sure, here's `curl -v https://private.redwood.acme.internal/health` from one app node (redacted IPs):
```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private.redwood.acme.internal/health
*   Trying 10.0.5.21...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to private.redwood.acme.internal (10.0.5.21) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate:
*  subject: CN=private.redwood.acme.internal
*  start date: Jan 30 00:00:00 2026 GMT
*  expire date: Feb 28 23:59:59 2027 GMT
*  issuer: C=US, O=ExampleCA, CN=Example Intermediate CA
*  SSL certificate verify result: unable to get local issuer certificate (20), continuing anyway.
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood.acme.internal
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*

< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: 9c1a-...

```

elaine: Thanks — that output smells like a missing intermediate in the chain. When you rotated, did you upload a full-chain (leaf + intermediates) or just the leaf? Can you also run `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.internal:443 -showcerts` and paste the cert count?

acme-sre: We used the rotator tool (internal) and IIRC just uploaded the PEM from our CA which is the leaf. `openssl s_client -showcerts` returned only one certificate (no intermediate blocks).

ravi: That would explain it. Two likely failure modes: 1) the rotator accepted the leaf but didn't attach the intermediate (UI/CLI bug), or 2) the rotator/reloader tried to fetch intermediates from the CA, but our VPC egress rules blocked the outbound fetch (OCSP/CRL and intermediate downloads).

opsbot: deploy 2026-01-30T13:11:22 - rotated cert for tenant acme-corp (job id: rot-7812), status=success

deploy-bot: reloader-service: "failed to fetch issuer cert: dial tcp 93.184.216.34:443: i/o timeout"

sam: That deploy-bot message is the smoking gun. The reloader marked the job success but couldn't fetch issuer cert due to outbound timeouts. Can you check your egress allowlist/firewall for outbound 443 to CA distribution endpoints?

acme-sre: We locked down egress last week to specific vendors. How do we find the exact hosts the reloader needs? We don't want to open 0.0.0.0/0.

elaine: From the rotator logs the reloader tries the CA's intermediate URL and OCSP: `https://crt.exampleca.com/intermediate.pem` and `https://ocsp.exampleca.com/`. Either allow those FQDNs (or resolved IPs) on port 443, or upload a concatenated chain to the tenant cert UI/CLI as a short-term fix. Also note the reloader performs OCSP stapling fetches which need egress too.

acme-sre: I uploaded the concatenated chain (leaf + intermediate) via the CLI and then restarted our private ingress: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-ingress` and cleared the TLS session cache. After that `curl -v` shows:
```
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate:
*  subject: CN=private.redwood.acme.internal
*  issuer: C=US, O=ExampleCA, CN=Example Intermediate CA
*  SSL certificate verify result: ok
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

sam: Nice. For follow-ups: 1) we should make rotator/reloader surface a partial-fail when intermediates can't be fetched instead of marking success, 2) we'll add CA hostnames to the Private deployment docs under "Egress requirements", and 3) advise customers to upload full chains if they plan to lock egress.

elaine: I've opened infra/rotator#492 to change success criteria and add clearer error messaging in the UI (cc @ravi).

ravi: On it — I'll add a log line with the exact URL attempt and the DNS resolution so customers can map to their allowlist entries. Will try to ship a patch this week.

acme-sre: Thanks everyone — we'll hold off on tightening egress for other tenants until we've updated rules and docs. :thumbsup:
